questions.q: Two vectors $\overset{→}{X}$ and $\overset{→}{Y}$ have equal magnitude. The magnitude of $( \overset{→}{X} - \overset{→}{Y} )$ is $n$ times the magnitude of $( \overset{→}{X} + \overset{→}{Y} )$. The angle between $\overset{→}{X}$ and $\overset{→}{Y}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given $X = Y$

$\sqrt{X^{2} + Y^{2} - 2 \times Ycos\theta}$

$= n\sqrt{X^{2} + Y^{2} + 2 \times Ycos\theta}$

Square both sides

$2X^{2} ( 1 - cos\theta ) = n^{2} \cdot 2X^{2} ( 1 + cos\theta )$

$1 - cos\theta = n^{2} + n^{2}cos\theta$

$cos\theta = \dfrac{1 - n^{2}}{1 + n^{2}}$

$\theta = \cos^{- 1} \left[\dfrac{n^{2} - 1}{- n^{2} - 1}]$

questions.q: Two vectors $\overset{→}{A}$ and $\overset{→}{B}$ have equal magnitudes. The magnitude of  \left(\overset{→}{A} + \overset{→}{B}\right)$ is ' $n$ ' times the magnitude of  \left(\overset{→}{A} - \overset{→}{B}\right)$ . The angle between $\overset{→}{A}$ and $\overset{→}{B}$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:& \left|\overset{→}{A} + \overset{→}{B}\right| = n\left|\overset{→}{A} - \overset{→}{B}\right|$, so, the magnitudes of this will be given as,

$\sqrt{A^{2} + B^{2} + 2ABcos\theta} = n \left(\sqrt{A^{2} + B^{2} - 2ABcos\theta}\right);where~\theta~is~the angle between~$\overset{→}{A}$~and~$\overset{→}{B}$.

Also,~\left|\overset{→}{A}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{B}\right|,

\sqrt{2A^{2} + 2A^{2}cos\theta} =$n$\sqrt{2A^{2} - 2A^{2}cos\theta}

Squaring both sides:

$2A^{2} \left(1 + cos\theta\right) = n^{2}2A^{2} \left($1 - cos$\theta\right)

cos\theta = \dfrac{n^{2} - 1}{n^{2} + 1}

i.e., \theta = \cos^{- 1} \left[\dfrac{n^{2} - 1}{n^{2} + 1}\right]

$

questions.q: If two vectors& $\overset{→}{P} = \overset{^}{i} + 2m\overset{^}{j} + m\overset{^}{k}$~ and~$\overset{→}{Q} = 4\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + m\overset{^}{k}$~ are perpendicular to each other. Then, the value of $m$ will be&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For two vectors to be perpendicular, their dot& product is equal to zero.

So,& $\overset{→}{P} \cdot \overset{→}{Q} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\overset{^}{i} + 2m\overset{^}{j} + m\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + m\overset{^}{k}\right) = 0 ⇒ 4 - 4m + m^{2} = 0 ⇒ \left(m - 2\right)2 = 0 ⇒ m = 2$

questions.q: A torque meter is calibrated to reference standards of mass, length and time each with $5 %$ accuracy. After calibration, the measured torque with this torque meter will have net accuracy of&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Dimensional formula for Torque

\left[τ\right] = \left[{ML}^{2}T^{- 2}\right]$

Now the percentage error in torque can be calculated by

$τ % = \left(1 \times $\dfrac{∆ M}{M} +$2 \times $\dfrac{∆ L}{L} +$2 \times $\dfrac{∆ T}{T}\right) \times$100 ⇒ τ % = 25 %$

$

questions.q: If two vectors $\overset{→}{A}$ and $\overset{→}{B}$ having equal magnitude $R$ are inclined at an angle $\theta$, then
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The magnitude of resultant vector $\overset{→}{A} + \overset{→}{B}$ is given by,

$R ' = \sqrt{A^{2} + B^{2} + 2ABcos\theta}$

Here $A = B = R$

Then $R ' = \sqrt{R^{2} + R^{2} + 2R^{2}cos\theta}$

$= R\sqrt{2}\sqrt{1 + cos\theta}$

$= \sqrt{2}R\sqrt{2\cos^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}}$

$= 2Rcos\dfrac{θ}{2}$

questions.q: The energy of a system is given as $\mathrm{E}(\mathrm{t})=\alpha^3 \mathrme^{-\beta t}$, where t is the time and $\beta=0.3 \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. The errors in the measurement of $\alpha$ and $t$ are $1.2 \%$ and $1.6 \%$, respectively. At $t=5 \mathrm{~s}$, maximum percentage error in the energy is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& d E=3 \alpha^2 d \alpha e^{-\beta t}+\alpha^3 e^{-\beta t}(-\beta) d t \\
& \frac{d E}{E}=\frac{3 d \alpha}{\alpha}+(-\beta) d t \\
& \frac{\Delta E}{E}=\frac{3 \Delta \alpha}{\alpha}+\beta \Delta t
\end{aligned}$
(\%) $\Delta t=1.6 \% \times 5=8 \%\%\left(\frac{3 \Delta \alpha}{\alpha}\right)=3 \times 1.2 \%=3.6 \%$
Putting values we get
$\Rightarrow 3.6+8 \times 0.3=6 \%$

questions.q: Two forces having magnitude $A$~and $\dfrac{A}{2}$& are perpendicular to each other. The magnitude of their resultant is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using parallelogram law of vector addition, the formula can be written as

${A}_{net} = \sqrt{{A1}^{2} + A^{2}2 + 2{A}_{1}{A}_{2}cos\theta}$

The data given is~

\left|\overset{→}{A1}\right| = A, \left|\overset{→}{A2}\right| = \dfrac{A}{2}$

Since the vectors are perpendicular~$\cos 90 ° = 0$

$⇒ {F}_{net} = \sqrt{A^{2} + \dfrac{A2}{4}}= \dfrac{\sqrt{5}A}{2}$

$

questions.q: Which of the following relations is true for two unit vector $\overset{^}{A}$ and $\overset{^}{B}$ making an angle $\theta$& to each other?

questions.solution:
We know,

& $1 - cos\theta = 2\sin^{2} \left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)1 + cos\theta ==2\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)

Now,\left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$2 + 2\overset{→}{a} $\cdot \overset{→}{b} + \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|$2 ⇒ \left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) = \left($1\right)2 + 2 \times1 \times1 \timescos\theta + \left(1\right)2 ⇒ \left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right) =$2\left($1 + cos$\theta\right)$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right|$2 = 4\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} + \overset{→}{b}\right| =$2\cos \left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) . . . ($1 )$

Similarly,

\left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right) = \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|$2 - 2\overset{→}{a} $\cdot \overset{→}{b} + \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|$2 ⇒ \left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right) = \left($1\right)2 - 2 $\times$1 $\times$1 $\times$cos$\theta + \left($1\right)2 ⇒ \left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right) =2\left(1 - cos\theta\right)⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right|2 = 4\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right)⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right| =2\sin \left(\dfrac{θ}{2}\right) . . . (2 )$

Therefore,

\left|\overset{^}{A} - \overset{^}{B}\right| = \left|\overset{^}{A} + \overset{^}{B}\right|\dfrac{tan\theta}{2}$

questions.q:
For the four sets of three measured physical quantities as given below. Which of the following options is correct?
\left(i\right){A}_{1} = 24.36, {B}_{1} = 0.0724, {C}_{1} = 256.2$
\left(ii\right){A}_{2} = 24.44, {B}_{2} = 16.082, {C}_{2} = 240.2$
\left(iii\right){A}_{3} = 25.2, {B}_{3} = 19.2812, {C}_{3} = 236.183$
\left(iv\right){A}_{4} = 25, {B}_{4} = 236.191, {C}_{4} = 19.5$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In addition or subtractions, final answer must contain the equal numbers of digits after decimal as the adding or subtracting quantities among& which is having the lowest numbers of digits after decimal.

${A}_{1} + {B}_{1} + {C}_{1} = 24.36 + 0.0724 + 256.2 = 280.6324 = 280 . 6$

The Least number of~ significant digit after decimal~ in the above expression is 1 So, Sum should conatian 1 significant digit after decimal.
${A}_{2} + {B}_{2} + {C}_{2} = 24.44 + 16.082 + 240.2 = 280.722 = 280.7$

The Least number of~ significant digit after decimal~ in the above expression is 1 So, Sum should conatian 1 significant digit after decimal
${A}_{3} + {B}_{3} + {C}_{3} = 25.2 + 19.2812 + 236.183 = 280.6642 = 280 . 7$

The Least number of~ significant digit after decimal~ in the above expression is 1 So, Sum should conatian 1 significant digit after decimal${A}_{4} + {B}_{4} + {C}_{4} = 25 + 236.191 + 19.5 = 280.691 = 281$

The Least number of~ significant digit after decimal~ in the above expression is 0 So, Sum should conatian~0 significant digit after decimal
Answer should be ${A}_{1} + {B}_{1} + {C}_{1} < {A}_{2} + {B}_{2} + {C}_{2} = {A}_{3} + {B}_{3} + {C}_{3} < {A}_{4} + {B}_{4} + {C}_{4}$

questions.q: In an octagon $ABCDEFGH$~of equal side, what is the sum of~$\overset{→}{AB} + \overset{→}{AC} + \overset{→}{AD} + \overset{→}{AE} + \overset{→}{AF} + \overset{→}{AG} + \overset{→}{AH},$~if, $\overset{→}{AO} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know,

$∵ \overset{→}{OA} + \overset{→}{OB} + \overset{→}{OC} + \overset{→}{OD} + \overset{→}{OE} + \overset{→}{OF} + \overset{→}{OG} + \overset{→}{OH} = \overset{→}{0}$

By triangle law of vector addition, we can write

$\overset{→}{AB} = \overset{→}{AO} + \overset{→}{OB}; \overset{→}{AC} = \overset{→}{AO} + \overset{→}{OC}$

$\overset{→}{AD} = \overset{→}{AO} + \overset{→}{OD}; \overset{→}{AE} = \overset{→}{AO} + \overset{→}{OE}$

$\overset{→}{AF} = \overset{→}{AO} + \overset{→}{OF}; \overset{→}{AG} = \overset{→}{AO} + \overset{→}{OG}$

$\overset{→}{AH} = \overset{→}{AO} + \overset{→}{OH}$

Now

$\overset{→}{AB} + \overset{→}{AC} + \overset{→}{AD} + \overset{→}{AE} + \overset{→}{AF} + \overset{→}{AG} + \overset{→}{AH}$

$= \left(7\overset{→}{AO}\right) + \overset{→}{OB} + \overset{→}{OC} + \overset{→}{OD} + \overset{→}{OE} + \overset{→}{OF} + \overset{→}{OG} + \overset{→}{OH}$

$= \left(7\overset{→}{AO}\right) + \overset{→}{0} - \overset{→}{OA}$

$= \left(7\overset{→}{AO}\right) + \overset{→}{AO}$

$= 8\overset{→}{AO} = 8 \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= 16\overset{^}{i} + 24\overset{^}{j} - 32\overset{^}{k}

$

questions.q: A vector has magnitude same as that of $\overset{→}{A} = 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{j}$ and is parallel to $\overset{→}{B} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$. The $x$ and $y$ components of this vector in first quadrant are $x$ and $3$ respectively where x =____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnitude of vector \left|\overset{→}{A}\right| = \sqrt{{3}^{2} + {4}^{2}} = 5$

Now, unit vector along $\overset{→}{B} = \dfrac{( 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} )}{{4}^{2} + {3}^{2}} = \dfrac{4}{5}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{3}{5}\overset{^}{j}$

Now, $\overset{→}{N} = \left|\overset{→}{A}\right|\overset{^}{B} = 5 \times \left(\dfrac{4}{5}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{3}{5}\overset{^}{j}\right) = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$

$∴ x = 4$

$

questions.q: Three particles $P, Q$ and $R$ are moving along the vectors $\overset{→}{A} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}, \overset{→}{B} = \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and~$\overset{→}{C} = - \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$,~respectively. They strike on a point and start to move in different directions. Now particle $P$ is moving normal to the plane which contains vector $\overset{→}{A}$ and $\overset{→}{B} .$~Similarly particle $Q$ is moving normal to the plane which contains vector $\overset{→}{A}$ and $\overset{→}{C} .$~The angle between the direction of motion of $P$ and $Q$ is $\cos^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) .$~Then the value of $x$& is .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Direction of& $P, \overset{^}{v}1 = \pm \dfrac{\overset{→}{A} \times \overset{→}{B}}{| \overset{→}{A} \times \overset{→}{B} |} = \pm \dfrac{\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}}{3}$

Direction of~$Q, \overset{^}{v}2 = \pm \dfrac{\overset{→}{A} \times \overset{→}{C}}{| \overset{→}{A} \times \overset{→}{C} |} = \pm \dfrac{2\overset{^}{k}}{2} = \pm \overset{^}{k}$

Angle between $\overset{^}{v}1$ and~$\overset{^}{v}2$,

$\dfrac{\overset{^}{v}1 \cdot \overset{^}{v}2}{\left|\overset{^}{v}1\right|\left|\overset{^}{v}2\right|} = \dfrac{\pm \dfrac{1}{3}}{( 1 ) ( 1 )} = \pm \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ x = 3$

questions.q: If $\overset{→}{P} = 3\overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{3}\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{Q} = 4\overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{3}\overset{^}{j} + 2 . 5\overset{^}{k}$~ then, the unit vector in the direction of $\overset{→}{P} \times \overset{→}{Q}$ is $\dfrac{1}{x} ( \sqrt{3}\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 2\sqrt{3}\overset{^}{k} )$. The value of $x$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Unit vector in the direction of& $\overset{→}{P} \times \overset{→}{Q}\text{is}\overset{^}{n} = \dfrac{\overset{→}{P} \times \overset{→}{Q}}{| \overset{→}{P} \times \overset{→}{Q} |}$.

Here,~$\overset{→}{P} \times \overset{→}{Q} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & \sqrt{3} & 2 \\ 4 & \sqrt{3} & 2 . 5\end{cases}$\right| = \sqrt{3}\overset{^}{i}2 + \overset{^}{j}2 - \sqrt{3}\overset{^}{k}$

And~\left|\overset{→}{P} \times \overset{→}{Q}\right| = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)2 + \left(\sqrt{3}\right)2} = \sqrt{4} = 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{\overset{→}{P} \times \overset{→}{Q}}{| \overset{→}{P} \times \overset{→}{Q} |} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\sqrt{3}\overset{^}{i}$2 + \overset{^}{j}2 - $\sqrt{3}\overset{^}{k}\right)

=\dfrac{1}{4} ( \sqrt{3}\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} -$2$\sqrt{3}\overset{^}{k} )$⇒ x = 4$

questions.q: For $z = a^{2}x^{3}y\dfrac{1}{2}$, where '$a$' is a constant. If percentage error in measurement of~ '$x$' and '$y$' are $4 %$and $12 %$, respectively, then the percentage error for '$z$' will be _____%.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:& $z = a^{2}x^{3}y\dfrac{1}{2}$

Relative error is given by~

$\dfrac{∆ z}{z} = \left[$3 $\times \dfrac{∆ x}{x} + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{∆ y}{y}\right]

Now, maximum percentage error in~$z$~is~

\dfrac{∆ z}{z} \times$100 = \left[$3\left($4\right) + $\dfrac{1}{2}\left($2\right)\right]$\times$100$

$= 18 %$.

$

questions.q: The density of a solid metal sphere is diameter. The maximum error in the density of the sphere is& \left(\dfrac{x}{100}\right) % .$ If the relative errors in measuring the mass and the diameter are $6 . 0 %$~and~$1 . 5 %$~respectively, the value of~$x$ is $-
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$ρ = \dfrac{m}{\dfrac{4}{3}\pi\left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)3}$

$ρ = \dfrac{6m}{\pid^{3}}$

taking log

$ℓnρ = ℓnm - 3ℓnd$

Maximum error by differentiation

$\dfrac{dρ}{ρ} = \dfrac{dm}{m} + 3\dfrac{dd}{d}$

$\dfrac{dp}{ρ} = 6 + 3 \times 1 . 5$

$= 10 . 5 % = \dfrac{1050}{100} %$

Ans. $x = 1050$
